name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

# gh-1039: [CRAP] configLoader.loadProjectConfig (54) + common/buildEncodedConfig.buildEncodedConfig (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

# gh-1039: [CRAP] configLoader.loadProjectConfig (54) + common/buildEncodedConfig.buildEncodedConfig (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

# gh-1039: [CRAP] configLoader.loadProjectConfig (54) + common/buildEncodedConfig.buildEncodedConfig (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.

blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

Confirmed. The doc generator extracts `customParams.<key>` (static) and `customParams['key']` (bracket with literal) patterns. The refactored `loadCustomParamFnHook(target, customParams, key, exportKey)` accesses `customParams[key]` dynamically — a plain variable, not a string literal — so `branchNamingFnPath` and `prSearchFnPath` vanish from the generated docs. That's exactly what the docs diff shows (296 deletions removing those two keys everywhere). And docs-freshness CI fails because `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` + `git diff --exit-code` detects the stale docs.

So the docs-freshness CI failure is a direct, causal result of this PR's refactor. This is a BLOCKING finding — red CI. Fix options: (a) keep a discoverable static reference, e.g. `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` comment in the source (fragile, smells), or (b) regenerate and commit the docs — but that would remove legitimately-documented params, a behavior/doc regression: the docs would no longer list `branchNamingFnPath`/`prSearchFnPath` as supported customParams even though they're still supported features. (c) Update agentDocGenerator regex — out of scope. The cleanest in-scope fix: the static analysis only scans JS action files referenced from agent JSONs; configLoader.js is referenced by actions. The best minimal fix preserving docs AND CI: call sites could use literal property access that the regex catches, e.g. inside loadCustomParamFnHook use `customParams[key]`... hmm.

```js
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams, customParams.branchNamingFnPath ? 'branchNamingFnPath' : '', 'branchNamingFn');
```

```js
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, { path: customParams.branchNamingFnPath }, ...

name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

# gh-1039: [CRAP] configLoader.loadProjectConfig (54) + common/buildEncodedConfig.buildEncodedConfig (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:
function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFn');
```

or add a `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` marker comment if you prefer to keep the current helper shape (regexes also match comments' text only when written as real member access — a plain comment with `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` in it does match the first regex, but the explicit-argument form above is less fragile). Then re-run `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` and confirm `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` is clean.

💡 **SUGGESTION: duplicated / orphaned `buildEncodedConfig` JSDoc block**

The full docblock for `buildEncodedConfig` (`Build the encoded config payload for a workflow dispatch.…`) appears twice in a row here: the first copy is orphaned (it documents a function that is defined ~200 lines later and doesn't match the helper that follows, `resolveProjectKey`), immediately followed by the same block again above the real function plus the correct `resolveProjectKey` doc. Delete the first copy.

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).

name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

# gh-1039: [CRAP] configLoader.loadProjectConfig (54) + common/buildEncodedConfig.buildEncodedConfig (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments.
